subject: psychology

moments.title: The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two
moments.body: Miller's paper synthesises decades of data on absolute judgement and immediate memory, proposing a capacity limit around seven items.

quote.text: My problem is that I have been persecuted by an integer.

moments.takeaway: Disparate experimental traditions converge on a common capacity limit.

moments.title: Plans and the Structure of Behaviour
moments.body: TOTE units (test-operate-test-exit), an early information-processing model of action.
moments.takeaway: Cybernetic ideas re-entered psychology through the cognitive revolution.

moments.title: Cowan's magical number four
moments.body: Cowan argues the true capacity, when controlling for chunking and rehearsal, is closer to four.
moments.takeaway: Even foundational numbers get revised by tighter methodology.

now.title: Capacity limits in instructional design
now.body: Cognitive load theory, multimedia learning principles and UX design all reference working memory limits.
now.open_questions: How does individual variation in capacity affect equity in instructional design?

reflection: Miller's paper is famous partly for its style; he opens with persecution by a number.
